claim: The Visitor's household, choices, objects and callbacks are explicitly invented illustrations; no exact household budget, occupation, address or survival probability is claimed.
locator: Editorial framing; spoken reconstruction disclaimer in opening
limit: Do not turn the hypothetical Visitor into an attested1709 person.

claim: The narrative begins in Paris in January1709 and follows the crisis into spring and August;1709's exceptional cold did not remain uninterrupted all winter.
locator: Météo-France temperature/calibration section; Morin analysis discussion
limit: Exact day-to-day timeline uses observations, not Saint-Simon's compressed rhetorical duration.

claim: Morin made repeated Paris weather observations; modern researchers interpret early nonstandard measurements. The record shows severe cold interrupted by milder periods.
locator: Morin methods and historical measurements; Météo-France opening weather sections
limit: No invented thermometer scale or unsupported numeric graph; use categorical sequence only.

claim: Saint-Simon reports frozen rivers and pieces of ice falling from bottles at a Versailles supper despite nearby fires.
limit: Attribute the anecdote to Saint-Simon and label Versailles; not every home, all drinks or guaranteed literal conditions everywhere.

claim: Ice and difficult routes disrupted the movement of provisions and wood; a city's fuel and food relied on deliveries.
locator: Van der Cruysse quotation on frozen watercourses and difficult roads
limit: Disruption, not total halt of every route for every day. No invented cart journey or quantified fuel cost.

claim: Saint-Simon describes rising bread prices, hoarding of existing grain and fear for the next harvest after frost damage.
limit: Keep attribution; do not validate all his accusations, a universal fixed price or a shortage conspiracy.

claim: Repeated frost and thaw damaged crops; replacement sowing of barley is documented as a response to lost wheat, with permission in April described by the historian.
locator: Saint-Simon chXLIV resown barley; Météo-France government-response section
limit: Barley helped; it did not erase famine or instantly feed everyone. No unsupported nationwide percentage.

claim: Relief included alms, soup distribution and public work; Saint-Simon describes people formerly able to give alms falling into need themselves.
limit: Availability/access varied; do not call it universal entitlement, copy1693 soup print as1709, or invent exact recipes/rations.

claim: Saint-Simon's account describes summer bread unrest and a20August bread shortage at boulevard earthworks paid with bread.
locator: ChXLIV Summer came and hillock between Portes SaintDenis/SaintMartin paragraphs
limit: Reported event, not all work schemes; show summer. No invented speech or graphic violence.

claim: France's continuing war formed part of the economic setting; harsh weather interacted with purchasing power, provisioning and relief rather than acting as an isolated inconvenience.
locator: ChXLIV exhausted finances and peace negotiations; Météo-France response/context
limit: Avoid attributing the whole crisis to a single cause or presenting1709 as trigger of1789.

claim: Being able to reach or afford food and fuel differs from their physical existence. A thaw cannot immediately replace a damaged harvest.
locator: Inference from price, transport and replacement-crop evidence above
limit: Explanatory reasoning, not a quantified model or statement every household faced identical choices.

claim: The crisis was lethal and access to resources and assistance mattered. A March 1709 contemporary account quoted by Le Roy Ladurie singles out children and older people without adequate protection.
locator: Saint-Simon ch. XLIV hunger/charity; Météo-France interview, quotation from La clef du cabinet, March 1709
limit: No casualty number, survival odds or graphic deaths are given.
